decisions.reason: The necessary cross-Requirement effect is already captured by the complete same-message MODIFY, which replaces optical drawing with proportional Hero V derivation and records proportional application of the selected terminal.
The source reaffirms the existing restrained hierarchy above the alphabet without changing the established 2% elevation or subordinate role.
The source's new two-column, six-option comparison protocol is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
Requiring the É accent to end at the Hero V peak restates the candidate's existing exact horizontal peak-alignment rule.
The source confines exploration to the Hero V terminal and explicitly leaves every other element unchanged; it does not alter the E or L letterform requirements.
Exact duplication of the Hero V right arm and direct inheritance of its eventual terminal treatment are already entailed by the candidate's literal derivation and exact vector-correspondence state.
The terminal's material-quality language concerns terminal geometry and character, not the selected Satin Reflection champagne-gold finish.
The instruction to keep established relationships locked and vary only the terminal already follows the candidate's existing preserve-all-locked-assets and single-variable revision policy.
The source does not change which wordmark elements receive champagne gold and directs that non-terminal elements remain unchanged.
The source does not revise the selected Balanced Flow kerning and requires all non-terminal geometry to remain unchanged.
Peak-height reference guides are presentation aids and do not modify the existing shared lower-baseline alignment requirement.
The new visual presentation protocol neither changes nor removes the existing requirement to explain each concept's design rationale.
